brief.headline: A new session finally printed and it delivered a genuine contradiction rather than a confirmation: the price rebounded $26 to $3,272 while the front-end premium was extinguished completely to a flat $0.00 spread, and on the same day the Chinese inventory draw that had been the bulls' best corroborating evidence collapsed from 12,000 tonnes to 500 tonnes week-on-week - so exchange stock has now fallen for 34 straight sessions to a fresh cycle low while nobody on the curve is willing to pay a cent for prompt metal.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: THE PRICE WENT UP AND THE CURVE WENT FLAT, WHICH IS AN ODD COMBINATION AND IS THE STORY OF THE DAY. The 17-August official cash settlement is $3,272.00, up $24.00 (+0.74%) from $3,248.00, breaking a three-session decline. But the three-month rose MORE, up $26.00 (+0.80%) to the identical $3,272.00, so the cash-3M spread went to EXACTLY ZERO from a $2.00 backwardation. Buyers paid up for forward metal and declined to pay up for prompt metal. This dashboard set a specific public test yesterday - a third backwardation makes it a trend, a contango marks it as noise - and the honest answer is neither: the premium was surrendered without the curve inverting.

WHY IT MATTERS: THE TWO STRONGEST BULLISH FACTS ON THIS BOARD JUST STARTED DISAGREEING WITH EACH OTHER. LME warrant drew another 1,375 tonnes to 246,925 tonnes - a 34th consecutive daily decline and a fresh low for this cycle - yet the prompt premium is now zero. An inventory series falling for seven straight weeks describes a market short of units; a flat curve describes a market that will not pay for one today. Both numbers are official and both come from the same board. The most defensible reading is that warrant is leaving warehouses for reasons that do not create prompt urgency, and that reading got materially stronger overnight.

THE EVIDENCE THAT WEAKENED: CHINA'S DESTOCKING ALL BUT STOPPED. SMM's 17-August spot commentary reports aluminium ingot inventory in China's major consumption areas down only 500 tonnes week-on-week, with Gongyi actually building stock - against a 12,000 tonne draw at the previous publication. SMM had warned the pace would slow in the second half of the month; it did, by roughly twenty-fold in one week. The 'two independent inventory pools drawing together' argument, which was the single best bullish datapoint available a day ago, is now carried by one pool. The same note has central China spot trading at a RMB 90-110 per tonne discount to the September contract with the procurement sentiment index down again week-on-week.

WHAT TO WATCH: TODAY'S RING, AND WHETHER THE CURVE FOLLOWS THE PRICE OR THE PRICE FOLLOWS THE CURVE. Two levels frame it. On the downside the swing low at $3,229.50 held on 17-August and remains the single explicit technical invalidation, now $42.50 below settlement. On the upside $3,292 is the 38.2% retracement of the decline off the $3,374 high and is the first level the market has not yet reclaimed. Alongside that, a base-metals complex that has stopped moving together is worth more attention than the aluminium tape alone: copper's prompt premium exploded to $535 on a day its inventory BUILT, zinc's narrowed on a day its inventory drew, and aluminium's vanished on a day its inventory hit a cycle low. Whatever set the front end of this complex on 17-August, warehouse stock was not it.

lme.commentary: THE 17-AUGUST RING PRINTED AND IT PRODUCED THE MOST INTERNALLY CONTRADICTORY BOARD OF THE CYCLE. Cash settled $3,272.00, up $24.00 (+0.74%) on the 14-August official of $3,248.00, breaking a three-session decline and cutting the give-back from the 11-August high of $3,373.00 to $101.00 (-2.99%). The three-month settled $3,272.00, up $26.00 (+0.80%). BECAUSE THE THREE-MONTH ROSE MORE THAN CASH IN DOLLAR TERMS, THE CASH-3M SPREAD WENT TO EXACTLY ZERO from a $2.00 backwardation. CONVENTION STATED EXPLICITLY: cash above three-month is BACKWARDATION, cash below is CONTANGO; today it is neither, and calling a flat curve by either name would be wrong. THIS IS THE THIRD CONSECUTIVE SESSION IN WHICH SPREAD AND FLAT PRICE MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, and today they did so in the bearish configuration: price up, prompt premium down to nothing. Length returning to a market normally tightens the prompt date. Here it did not, which says the buying was expressed in forward tenors. MEANWHILE THE STOCK LINE DID THE OPPOSITE OF THE CURVE: warrant drew 1,375 tonnes to 246,925 tonnes, the 34th consecutive daily decline and a fresh cycle low, down 22,375 tonnes (-8.31%) from 269,300 tonnes on 28-July. Those two facts cannot both be describing the same physical condition and this dashboard will not pretend otherwise. Note also that the draw itself is decelerating - 1,375 tonnes is the smallest of the fifteen-session window against a 1,492-tonne average. THE TECHNICAL TEST SET YESTERDAY WAS PASSED ON ONE LEG AND FAILED ON THE OTHER: the wave (iv) low at $3,229.50 held comfortably, with cash settling $42.50 above it, so the impulse-continuation count survives; but the backwardation did not reach a third session, so the tightening-independently-of-positioning thesis did not get its confirmation. AN INDEPENDENT SERIES DID NOT CORROBORATE BECAUSE IT HAD NOT ROLLED: Trading Economics' aluminium CFD still marked $3,247.70 for 14-August at this compile even though its zinc, nickel and lead rows had already updated to 17-August. That is a lag in one vendor's feed, not a dispute about price, and it is reported here rather than quietly ignored.

The three-month rose more than cash in dollar terms, so the bid was for forward metal, not prompt metal.

prices.label: Alumina FOB East Australia (SMM reported trade)
prices.note: HELD AT $356/mt FOB EAST AUSTRALIA (SMM-reported transaction of 30,000 mt for September loading dealt 05-Aug-2026, published 06-Aug). NO PUBLIC SEABORNE ALUMINA PRICE PRINT DATED AFTER THE ALUNORTE EPISODE HAS BEEN FOUND AT THIS COMPILE, SO NO VALUE ON THIS PANEL IS CHANGED FOR A FIFTH RUN - the events are recorded, the price is not invented. This is a Sunday compile and seaborne alumina transactions are not reported at the weekend, so the absence is expected rather than surprising. THE SUPPLY EVENT RESOLVED AND HAS STAYED RESOLVED. Norsk Hydro announced on 13-August that Alunorte in Barcarena, Para - 6.3 Mt/y nameplate and the largest alumina refinery outside China - is ramping back to FULL capacity after Brazil's regulator ANP approved it as a self-importer of natural gas and a temporary terminal-access agreement was reached with gas supplier CELBA. The disruption ran three days from the 11-August disclosure of a cut to 50%. Lost production is put at 100,000-120,000 tonnes with a guided potential Q3-2026 Bauxite & Alumina impact of US$75-100 million. No newer development published over the weekend. THE HONEST READ REMAINS THAT THE COST CONSEQUENCE WAS NEVER OBSERVED: the outage never lasted long enough to produce a public seaborne price print and now probably never will. Roughly 3 Mt/y annualised off the balance for three days is a rounding error against a 145 Mt/y global market. THE OTHER RECENT PRINT, STATED SEPARATELY BECAUSE THE BASIS DIFFERS AND MUST NOT BE BLENDED: SMM published on 11-August that 30,000 mt traded at $365/mt CIF MALAYSIA for September shipment, dealt 07-Aug-2026. CIF Malaysia is a delivered price including freight; FOB East Australia is a load-port price, so the $9/mt gap is broadly freight rather than a rally. MARGIN CONTEXT AT AN UNCHANGED METAL PRICE: against the 14-August three-month official of $3,246.00 the FOB mark sits at about 11.0% of the metal price and the CIF mark at about 11.2%, both unchanged from yesterday because neither leg moved. Both remain well below the decade rule of thumb of roughly 15-17%, so the alumina leg is still a clear TAILWIND to smelter economics. NEW CONTEXT FROM THE GULF THIS WEEKEND: SMM reports that the Gulf producer's alumina refinery recovered to 50% of pre-incident capacity in early July after its H1-2026 production fell significantly year-on-year - a second refinery returning supply to a market that has just absorbed the Alunorte scare without printing a price.

THE MOST USEFUL RECENT CHINESE ALUMINA DATAPOINT REMAINS A COST NUMBER, NOT A PRICE: SMM published on 11-August that China's national weighted-average FULL production cost for alumina was RMB 2,718/mt in July, UP RMB 37/mt month-on-month, with the weighted-average CASH cost at RMB 2,544/mt. SMM guides August full cost to RMB 2,700-2,820/mt and cash cost to RMB 2,530-2,650/mt. The rise is attributed almost entirely to bauxite - higher imported CIF costs on elevated ocean freight plus the Guinea rainy season, and persistently tight domestic ore after mining-accident after-effects slowed restarts - partly offset by a small decline in energy costs. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY THIS CREATES WITH THE ALUNORTE EVENT: China's alumina cost floor is rising for domestic reasons at the same time as roughly 3 Mt/y of non-Chinese seaborne supply sits at half rate. The two are independent and they push the same way.

notes: ALUNORTE IS BACK AND HAS STAYED BACK - NO NEW DEVELOPMENT OVER THE WEEKEND. THE WORD THAT STILL MATTERS IN THE COMPANY'S OWN LANGUAGE IS 'TEMPORARY'. The terminal-access agreement with CELBA is explicitly temporary and sits alongside regulatory approval for the refinery to act as a self-importer of natural gas. The outage is resolved on a run-rate basis but the underlying gas arrangement is not permanently settled. A 6.3 Mt/y refinery is large enough that any recurrence is material to the seaborne balance, so the thing to watch is a further disclosure converting the temporary arrangement into a durable one - or failing to.

THE EPISODE PASSED WITHOUT REGISTERING ON ANY PUBLIC PRICE SERIES, AND THAT IS ITSELF THE FINDING. No public seaborne alumina transaction dated after 07-August has been located across five consecutive runs. Three days of a 3 Mt/y annualised outage is about 50-60 kt on a pro-rata basis, reconciling broadly with the company's own 100-120 kt figure for the full reduced-rate period, against a roughly 145 Mt/y global market. The prior expectation stated here so it could be checked - that the episode would leave no mark - has so far held.

A SECOND REFINERY IS ALSO RETURNING, WHICH IS THE NEW ALUMINA FACT OF THE WEEKEND. SMM's 16-August review discloses that the Gulf producer's alumina refinery recovered to 50% of pre-incident levels in early July, after H1-2026 production fell significantly year-on-year. Alumina supply is therefore being restored from two directions at once while the metal price falls, which is why the alumina-to-metal ratio remains a tailwind to smelter margin rather than a threat to it.

THE STRUCTURAL COST PRESSURE THAT SURVIVES ALL OF THIS IS BAUXITE, NOT ALUMINA. SMM's cost work identifies imported bauxite as the core driver of the rise in Chinese alumina full production cost in July, citing elevated ocean freight and the Guinea rainy season reducing shipments alongside slow domestic Chinese mine resumption. That pressure is about ore supply and freight rather than about any single refinery's gas contract, so it is unaffected by the Alunorte resolution and remains the best-evidenced upward-trending input on this board.

ALUNORTE'S RETURN HAS ALREADY REPRICED EQUITIES, NOT JUST METAL. AL Circle reports that Norsk Hydro's resumption of higher alumina production at the 6.3 Mt/y Alunorte refinery eased raw-material concerns and weighed on Indian aluminium producers' shares, with the Indian contract settling 1.73% lower at INR 346.80. The only credible alumina cost threat of the year lasted three days.

NO INTERIM DIVIDEND FOR H1-2026 AT THE LARGEST NON-CHINESE, NON-WESTERN PRODUCER. Ahead of today's board meeting to approve H1-2026 IFRS accounts, the board has recommended shareholders decide not to declare or pay a first-half dividend. Read against a peer group reporting record revenues and sharply higher realised prices, a withheld distribution is a data point about where that producer sits on the cost curve and on cash generation - though dividend policy at that company has been irregular for years, so it is a signal to be weighted, not a verdict.

TARIFF-DRIVEN US REINDUSTRIALISATION IS MEETING LOCAL PERMITTING FRICTION: AL Circle reports Section 232 support is encouraging new US aluminium manufacturing while a proposed Oklahoma smelter faces local opposition. The western supply response tracked here is a schedule of announcements, and permitting is the most common reason such schedules slip to the right.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

THE 05-AUG IRAN-OMAN AGREEMENT ON ROUTE COORDINATES IS THE FIRST CONCRETE STEP TOWARD A REOPENING, and it is deliberately NOT treated as one here: the route is temporary (two to four months by Iran's own account), both existing lanes would close in its favour, Tehran says safe navigation is not restored, and the published count on the day was eight vessels against roughly 130-140 pre-war. Kept at 'tightening' pending observable transit recovery. Even a full transit reopening leaves the production impairment in place for quarters.

flows.note: THE RED SEA IS DIVERGING FROM HORMUZ. Bab al Mandeb traffic fell to a weekly low of 16 commodity vessels on 26-Jul after the Houthi 'embargo' on Saudi shipping declared 20-Jul and claimed attacks on Aramco sites at Jizan and Yanbu, recovering only to 31 by 31-Jul. On 05-Aug Houthi forces claimed they had targeted a Saudi oil tanker in the Gulf of Aden and threatened further vessels in the Red Sea, with a ship reported hit the same day. A Hormuz routing agreement does not address this constraint. Saudi Arabia has been diverting crude to the Suez routing; the Suez leg for Gulf and Red Sea origin cargoes is therefore still not a clean alternative to Hormuz.

catalysts.text: TODAY'S LME OFFICIAL, AND AFTER YESTERDAY THE TEST HAS CHANGED. THE CURVE IS NOW THE QUESTION, NOT THE PRICE. The cash-3M spread went to EXACTLY ZERO on 17-August after two sessions of backwardation. A return to backwardation would say the two-day premium was a real physical signal interrupted; a slip into contango on a 35th consecutive stock draw would be the single most bearish structural print available on this board, because it would mean the market declines to pay for prompt metal even at a cycle-low inventory. SECOND, THE LEVELS. The wave (iv) low at $3,229.50 held on 17-August and remains the explicit short-term invalidation, now $42.50 below settlement; a decisive close beneath it promotes the bearish alternate and opens $3,205 and then $3,159.50. On the upside $3,292 is the 38.2% retracement of the fall from $3,374 and is the first level the market has NOT reclaimed - the 61.8% at $3,241 and the 50% at $3,267 were both taken back on 17-August. FOR THIRD-PARTY CALIBRATION ONLY, NOT ENDORSEMENT: SMM's published week-ahead range is $3,180-3,330 on LME and RMB 23,600-24,450 on the most-traded SHFE contract, and the price has moved into the upper half of that band.

TODAY: A MAJOR RUSSIAN PRODUCER'S BOARD MEETS TO APPROVE H1-2026 IFRS ACCOUNTS. The board of directors is scheduled to meet on 18-August-2026 to review first-half operational performance, committee reports and budget execution, and to consider and approve the consolidated interim condensed IFRS financial statements and interim report. ONE PUBLIC DETAIL IS ALREADY OUT AHEAD OF THE NUMBERS: the board has recommended that shareholders decide NOT to declare or pay a dividend for the first half of 2026. It is the next dated peer-earnings event and the first half-year read on the largest producer outside China and the West. The comparison base is public: adjusted EBITDA of US$748 million in H1-2025 against US$786 million in H1-2024, with the EBITDA margin narrowing from 13.8% to 9.9% and a shareholders' loss of US$87 million in H1-2025. Given realised prices across the peer group have risen sharply this year, the interest is in whether that margin compression has reversed - a read on where the industry cost curve actually sits at these metal prices.

THE MONTHLY CARBON SETTLEMENT WINDOW IS OPEN AND HAS NOT PRINTED. Prebaked anodes, coal tar pitch and green petroleum coke settle conventionally around the 17th-18th. A dedicated search this run returned no published August settlement for any of the three rows, all of which are carried at their June or July cycles and NONE OF WHICH WAS ESTIMATED. The directional risk into the window remains modestly upward on crude, and the fluoride lines have already moved that way - cryolite repriced up to RMB 7,500-9,000/t and the August aluminium fluoride tender raised RMB 250/t month-on-month - so a firm carbon settlement would make it two cost groups turning against smelters in the same fortnight. MJP Q4-2026 PREMIUM NEGOTIATIONS conventionally open against the Q3-2026 settlement of $395/t CIF Japan. A dedicated search this run again returned nothing dated after the 06-July settlement - no producer offers, no negotiation levels, no settlement coverage - so the pending quarter remains a SCENARIO RANGE of $305-395 and NOT an assessment. THE RANGE IS HELD UNCHANGED BUT THE BALANCE INSIDE IT MOVED TOWARD BUYERS ON 17-AUGUST, and the mechanism is specific rather than atmospheric: a seller's strongest argument in a premium negotiation is a backwardated front end, and that argument was live for two sessions and is now gone. Buyers additionally gained Chinese social inventory destocking collapsing to 500 tonnes week-on-week, a widening central China physical discount, and a research house saying the Gulf restart is beating expectations. Sellers retain 34 consecutive LME draws to a cycle low and a closed Strait. For reference, Q3 opening offers ran $440-480/t and settled at $395/t, and the CIF Japan spot reference sits $25/t below the settled quarterly number.

Where public numbers conflict and cannot be verified against a primary disclosure, the correct action is to publish nothing and say so. The earnings-history entry for that company therefore remains at three sourced points with the fourth left as a gap, and it will be filled from the company's own interim announcement when that is published. SMM BAUXITE WEEKLY REVIEW. The last edition carried here (06-August) had the SMM Imported Bauxite Index at $71.57/mt, up $0.70 week-on-week, with Guinea CIF at $70-74/mt and Guinea FOB at $38-42/mt. Bauxite is the identified core driver of the rise in Chinese alumina full production cost and remains the best-evidenced upward-trending input on this board - the structural cost pressure that survives the Alunorte resolution entirely, because it is about ore supply and freight rather than one refinery's gas contract. The August Guinea long-term contract remains under negotiation against July's $70-71.5/mt settlement, and Guinea's move to monthly spot tenders through state-owned Nimba Mining adds price discovery while shifting volume from contract to spot.

THE PERMANENCE OF THE ALUNORTE GAS ARRANGEMENT. Norsk Hydro's own language is that the terminal-access agreement with CELBA is TEMPORARY, alongside ANP approval for the refinery to act as a self-importer of natural gas. The outage is resolved on a run-rate basis but the underlying gas supply arrangement is not permanently settled, and a 6.3 Mt/y refinery is large enough that any recurrence is material to the seaborne alumina balance. The thing to watch is a further company disclosure converting the temporary arrangement into a durable one - or failing to. Note also that no public seaborne alumina print dated after 07-August has appeared across seven runs, so the entire episode passed without registering on any price series available here.

risks.text: SUPPLY RELIEF ARRIVES ON A DATED, PUBLISHED SCHEDULE AND CAPS THE RECOVERY. SMM's 16-August review states that 18% of the Gulf smelter's 1,262 pots have restarted, that the pace of resumption is FASTER THAN THE MARKET PREVIOUSLY EXPECTED, and that the previously traded tight-supply premium faces give-back pressure with upside room capped by resumption expectations. Sitting on top of that: Q1-2027 Gulf recovery guidance, the Australian smelter power settlement covering up to 590,000 t/y, Alunorte's return to full rate, Slovalco's 75,000 t/y in Q4-2026, Magnitude 7 Metals' 75,000 t/y before year-end, and Mount Holly already at full capacity adding nearly 10% to US primary output on its own. TREND UP, HIGH IMPACT AND UNCHANGED AS THE DOMINANT RISK ON THIS BOARD: this is not a forecast, it is a published schedule reported to be running ahead of itself. The one counterweight logged this run is that the same schedule can slip - AL Circle reported on 17-August that a proposed Oklahoma smelter faces local opposition, which is the ordinary way announcement schedules move right.

THE STOCK DRAW STOPS OR REVERSES AND REMOVES THE BULL CASE'S BEST EVIDENCE. TREND CHANGED TO UP THIS RUN, AND THE CHANGE IS DELIBERATE RATHER THAN COSMETIC. For a week this risk was trending DOWN because two structurally different inventory pools were drawing together. That stopped on 17-August. SMM's spot commentary puts Chinese aluminium ingot inventory in the major consumption areas down just 500 TONNES week-on-week, with Gongyi actually building stock, against a 12,000 tonne draw at the previous publication - a roughly twenty-fold deceleration in a single week, which SMM itself had forecast but not at that magnitude. The LME line also decelerated: the 1,375 tonne draw on 17-August was the SMALLEST of the fifteen-session window against a 1,492 tonne average. And the curve delivered the corroborating verdict on the same day by extinguishing the prompt premium entirely. THE BULL CASE RETAINS THE HEADLINE - 34 consecutive draws to a fresh cycle low of 246,925 tonnes - but it has lost the second pool and the curve confirmation in one session, and a large off-warrant stockpile changing hands for cash on 14-August is a reminder that visible warrant is a subset of the units in the system.

PROLONGED HORMUZ CLOSURE KEEPS GULF SUPPLY IMPAIRED. Day 170 since the shutdown. The most recent public restatement, in SMM's 16-August review, has the Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council saying the Strait will remain closed unless the United States changes its behaviour, with reopening conditional on the US meeting five conditions including a permanent halt to military operations; the US President is separately reported as preferring economic pressure to another large-scale military operation, and Iran's Foreign Minister says there are no negotiations under way though mediators continue trying. NOTHING DATED 17 OR 18-AUGUST CHANGED ANY OF THAT, AND A DEDICATED SEARCH THIS RUN FOUND NO NEWER DEVELOPMENT. TREND FLAT: the Strait is still shut and the substance is unchanged. The Gulf was around a tenth of global primary production pre-conflict, and last week supplied the calibration - repricing three individual assets moved this market 3.7% in three sessions, so a change in the Strait regime itself would be an order of magnitude larger in either direction.

PHYSICAL DEMAND WEAKENS AT THIS PRICE LEVEL, AND THE 17-AUGUST CHINESE SPOT DATA IS THE CLEAREST EVIDENCE YET. SMM reports central China transacting at a DISCOUNT of RMB 90-110 per tonne against the SHFE 09 contract, the central China procurement sentiment index falling a further 0.07 week-on-week to 2.9, downstream processors showing low stockpiling sentiment on the first day of the week, and the overall trading atmosphere described as 'sluggish'. That sits alongside three data points carried from the previous run and not superseded: China's July billet operating rate at a year-to-date high of 58.3% but with processing fees BELOW average production cost and the August rate expected to retreat to about 56.9%; CPCA data putting China's July passenger vehicle retail at 1.461 million units, down 20.9% year-on-year; and US July retail sales down 0.6% month-on-month with the core control group at its worst since January 2025. The one offset is genuine and is reported alongside: SMM's PV frame survey found operating rates stable with leading enterprises holding ample orders to month-end. TREND UP, HIGH IMPACT: the demand evidence is accumulating in the world's two largest consuming economies while the price sits $112.50 above the July swing low.

POSITIONING UNWIND IN A CROWDED LONG. TREND MOVED FROM DOWN TO FLAT THIS RUN BECAUSE THE 17-AUGUST SESSION CUT BOTH WAYS AND IT WOULD BE DISHONEST TO SCORE IT AS EITHER. Against the risk: the market rallied $26.00, the give-back from $3,374.00 narrowed to $101.00, the $3,229.50 swing low held comfortably, and SMM reported that in Friday's LME session volume pulled back while OPEN INTEREST INCREASED - bulls adding rather than length liquidating. For the risk: the rally was expressed entirely in forward tenors, taking the cash-3M spread to zero, which is what a rebuilding speculative position looks like rather than a physical short-cover. A long expressed in the forward curve while the prompt date goes bid-less is precisely the configuration that unwinds fastest when the supply schedule delivers. Residual exposure remains materially lower than it was at $3,374.00.

AN ALUMINA COST SHOCK RE-EMERGES. TREND DOWN. The Alunorte gas disruption - the only credible alumina cost threat of the year - resolved in three days via ANP self-import approval and a temporary CELBA terminal-access agreement, with lost production of 100,000-120,000 t against a roughly 145 Mt/y global market and no public seaborne price print produced at any point. AL Circle reported on 14-August that the resumption of higher output has already repriced Indian aluminium equities lower, with the Indian contract settling 1.73% down at INR 346.80 - the cost relief is being taken as real by markets other than this one. The Gulf producer's alumina refinery separately recovered to 50% of pre-incident capacity in early July, so supply is being restored from two directions. The carried FOB East Australia mark of $356/t is about 10.9% of the 17-August three-month price against a decade rule of thumb of 15-17%, leaving alumina a clear tailwind to smelter margin. THE RESIDUAL RISK IS THE WORD 'TEMPORARY' IN THE CELBA AGREEMENT, and the longer-run risk is upstream of the refinery - the thread running through the Guinea contract negotiations, the surge in Chinese alumina imports and the Jamaica-Ghana tolling proposal.

SMELTER ENERGY AND CARBON COSTS RE-INFLATE - AND THE MONTHLY SETTLEMENT WINDOW IS OPEN RIGHT NOW WITH NOTHING PUBLISHED. Prebaked anodes, coal tar pitch and green petroleum coke settle conventionally around the 17th-18th; a dedicated search this run returned NO August print for any of the three, so all three rows are carried at their June or July cycles and none has been estimated. Two things still point the settlement upward: crude has been firm, and green coke is a refinery by-product whose price follows crude with a lag; and the fluoride lines have ALREADY moved, with SMM's 16-August fluoride weekly lifting cryolite quotations to RMB 7,500-9,000/t from RMB 7,000-8,500/t, holding aluminium fluoride at RMB 11,200-11,800/t, and reporting the August AlF3 tender price of the benchmark Chinese enterprise raised RMB 250/t month-on-month on 97% fluorite firm at RMB 3,300-3,750/t. TREND UP: a firm carbon settlement this week would make it two cost groups turning against smelters in the same fortnight, at a moment when the metal has given back $101.00 from its high and the prompt premium has gone to zero.
